context:
Treat canary and ruleset drift as evidence freshness problems. First define
which evidence is required and how fresh it must be; then produce compact
artifacts; then make release PRs consume those artifacts. Keep live cloud
suites advisory unless credential and cost policy are explicitly resolved.
description:
The first release-required gate should stay focused enough to be reliable on
every release PR. That still leaves long-tail risk: slow/resource-heavy/stress
tests, live integration tests, scheduled cross-platform validation, and
GitHub ruleset drift can invalidate release confidence without blocking a
single release PR.

This TODO adds defense-in-depth:
  - a periodic canary that runs the broader non-fast suite families on a
    clear schedule,
  - a compact release-readiness check that fails release PRs when the latest
    required canary is stale or red,
  - a repository-visible ruleset drift check so comments about
    `main-release-only` and `develop-squash-only` do not silently diverge from
    live GitHub settings.

anti_patterns.dont: commit raw CI logs or screenshots as evidence
anti_patterns.why: release readiness needs compact durable summaries.

anti_patterns.instead: fail or require an explicit override.

anti_patterns.dont: use stale nightly success from a SHA that does not contain the release branch changes unless the release-readiness policy explicitly permits ancestor-based evidence.
wire a long full-suite run directly into every develop PR
anti_patterns.why: this defeats the current path-aware dev loop

deferrals.reason: Requires credential availability, cloud spend policy, and flake history; start with credential-free canary plus explicit live-test advisory status.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] non-actionable: Describes the rejected alternative (block release on all live cloud) versus the actual DONE solution (credential-free canary + advisory status).
deferrals.summary: Block every release on all live cloud integrations

deferrals.reason: Package indexes are immutable for version uploads; recovery should be patch release or incident process, not automated destructive action.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] non-actionable: Reason explicitly argues against the action: package indexes are immutable and automated destructive rollback is rejected in favor of manual incident process.
deferrals.summary: Automatically revert published releases on canary failure

preserves.behavior: Raw pytest, Docker, and live-test logs remain CI artifacts or `/tmp` files, not tracked source.
Release-readiness checks fail closed on stale evidence unless an explicit documented override path is used.
Routine develop PR latency remains governed by the lightweight PR gate; canary work runs scheduled/manual or release-readiness only.

prior_art.concept: .github/workflows/cross-platform-validation.yml:TPC-H SF=0.01 validation — reuse structured diff artifact pattern for canary evidence
.github/workflows/develop-post-merge.yml:auto-revert metrics — reuse compact workflow-summary style, not raw logs in git
.github/workflows/nightly.yml:scheduled validation — extend existing scheduled validation surface
docs/operations/repo-admin-settings.md:ruleset runbook — use as local expected-state source

work_units.notes:
Capture raw output under `/tmp/release-canary-ruleset-w0/` and commit only
a compact summary in PR body or TODO notes.

Required commands:
  - `rg -n "schedule:|cron:|workflow_dispatch:|integration:|test-all|test-slow|resource_heavy|stress" .github/workflows Makefile pytest.ini`
  - `BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK=1 uv run -- python -m pytest --collect-only -q -n 0 -m "slow or resource_heavy or stress"`
  - `BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK=1 uv run -- python -m pytest --collect-only -q -n 0 -m "live_integration"`
  - `sed -n '47,130p' docs/operations/repo-admin-settings.md`

Optional live ruleset verification, only with user authorization:
  - `gh api repos/joeharris76/BenchBox/rulesets --jq '.[] | {id, name, target}'`

Decision gate:
  - If slow/resource/stress collection is too large or unstable for one
    job, split the canary by suite family and make the readiness check
    require the configured subset, not an impossible monolith.

Implementation evidence:
  - Captured raw w0 output under `/tmp/release-canary-ruleset-w0/`.
  - `slow or resource_heavy or stress` collected 684/24780 tests.
  - `live_integration` collected 233/24780 tests.
  - Blocking credential-free canary expression
    `(slow or resource_heavy) and not (stress or live_integration)`
    collected 388/24780 tests.
  - Decision: make the first blocking canary daily, credential-free,
    serial, and freshness-gated at 48h. Keep stress and live suites
    advisory until runtime, credential, cost, and flake policy are stable.
  - Live GitHub ruleset API verification was not performed locally; drift
    detection is implemented as a scheduled/manual canary job and mocked
    unit tests.
work_units.summary: Re-validate current scheduled workflows, suite sizes, and ruleset runbook state

work_units.notes:
Document:
  - Which scheduled workflow(s) count as release canaries.
  - Maximum allowed age, initially 48h unless CI quota/runtime evidence
    says otherwise.
  - Which failures block release PRs.
  - Who can approve an emergency override and where that override is
    recorded.

Decision gate:
  - Do not add a release-readiness check until the stale/red behavior and
    emergency override semantics are documented.
work_units.summary: Define the canary freshness contract and override policy

work_units.notes:
Extend `nightly.yml` or add a dedicated workflow that runs:
  - slow + resource-heavy families serially or in bounded parallelism,
  - stress subset only if runtime/resource limits are acceptable,
  - selected live-integration/cross-platform jobs only when credentials
    and Docker/service constraints are stable.

Artifacts:
  - compact JSON summary with commit SHA, workflow name, job conclusions,
    suite families, collected counts, and completion time,
  - raw pytest logs only as CI artifacts, not committed files.

Decision gate:
  - If a dedicated workflow is needed, use the scoped name
    `.github/workflows/release-canary.yml`; do not add an unreviewed
    workflow filename outside `scope_limit`.
  - If live credentials are unavailable, explicitly mark live cloud tests
    advisory and keep the blocking canary to credential-free suites.
work_units.summary: Add scheduled non-fast canary workflow jobs with compact artifacts

work_units.notes:
Add a `validate-main-pr.yml` job or release-required workflow job that:
  - applies only to release PRs targeting `main`,
  - queries the latest successful configured canary run or reads a
    durable canary artifact,
  - fails if no canary is green within the freshness window,
  - reports the canary SHA and age in the job summary.

Decision gate:
  - Do not allow this job to silently pass when GitHub API queries fail.
    API failure is either blocking or requires an explicit documented
    emergency override.
work_units.summary: Add release-readiness check that fails release PRs on stale or red canary

work_units.notes:
Add a script or workflow check that compares live GitHub rulesets with
`docs/operations/repo-admin-settings.md`.

Required checks:
  - required status check contexts for `main` and `develop`,
  - strict-base settings,
  - bypass actor list,
  - linear history / non-fast-forward / deletion protections where
    documented.

Decision gate:
  - If live GitHub API access is unavailable in PR CI, make this a
    scheduled/manual workflow with a release-readiness artifact. Do not
    pretend local YAML alone proves external ruleset state.
work_units.summary: Add ruleset drift detection against the repository runbook
